note: The bands the E-flite Night Timber X 1.2m plant has to land in, from docs/NIGHTTIMBER-STAGE1.md, which derives each from E-flite's manual and product pages, its photographs, APC's data for the 13 x 4E prop and momentum theory (scripts/nighttimber-derive.js prints the derived figures). E-flite publishes no bench or flight figure, so the performance bands are about derived figures built on an ESTIMATED motor and drag, and each says how wide and why; the widths are the Extra's (tests/extra-thresholds.json) for the same reasons. Never widened to pass; argue in the derivation instead.

n1_level_75.source: level speed at 75 percent throttle, derived 12.34 from the estimated thrust line and drag polar; 12 percent either way. Derived 17.43 since then, re-derived 2026-10-11 on APC's 13 x 4E curve (prop curves, npm run prop:curves -- wings), was 12.34 on the straight line; the same 12 percent about it.. Re-derived 2026-10-11 again with the stick put through the electric motor's own law, n^2 + 5.667 n = 6.667 d (plant_wing.c prop_spool, scripts/lib/propcurve.js electricN): the derivation had flown the stick as the prop's speed share, which the plant has not held since its motor law changed; derived 18.09, was 17.43; the same 12 percent about it Re-derived 2026-10-12 on the gates' 4.1 V seat (w36-seat-voltage: the pack's loaded voltage over the table's v_meas through the motor's law, scripts/lib/propcurve.js wingSeat): derived 21.08, was 18.09; the same 0.880 to 1.120 of it (was 15.92 to 20.26).

n2_stall.source: flaps up: sqrt(2W / rho S CLmax), derived 9.08 at 1698 g on the clean 0.287 m^2 and the Turbo Timber's CLmax of 1.15; alphaStall is CLmax / CLalpha, 1.15 / 4.904. 0.94 to 1.14 of the formula, the Kadet's and the Extra's proportion, since the plant reads the stall at the blend's midpoint Re-derived 2026-10-11: alphaStall over the wing's own slope, a_w 4.494 (scripts/nighttimber-derive.js), not the wing and tail's 4.9038: the stall angle is the wing's and the tail's share lifts on past it, as the Extra's (#935); was 0.23451. And the band with it: the plant's CLmax is the wing's 1.150 plus the tail's lift at that angle, on its own angle, (CLa - a_w) (sin a - de/da a - a_0 (1 - de/da)) / (1 - de/da) = 0.091, so the formula's speeds go by sqrt(1.150 / 1.241) = 0.9626.

n2b_stall_flaps.source: full flaps, power off, the nose raised slowly (wingpilot.js stallSpeed, from 11 m/s as the Timber's T4): the real aircraft's own figure, the video's pilot's 15 to 18 mph, 6.7 to 8.0 m/s, with full flaps (analysis/3D-VIDEO-LESSONS.md 19:20). The derivation's sqrt(2W / rho S CLmax) with the plain flap's Raymer increment is 8.08, at the band's top: it leaves out the flap mix's down elevator and the tail's share, which the plant flies; since #854 (CL max at the top of the curve) the plant reads 7.3 at the linear crossing, alphaStall (CLmax + clmax_df df - dCL(df)) / CLalpha. Re-derived to the real aircraft on 2026-10-09 after #854, docs/NIGHTTIMBER-STAGE1.md Re-derived 2026-10-11: alphaStall over the wing's own slope, a_w 4.494 (scripts/nighttimber-derive.js), not the wing and tail's 4.9038: the stall angle is the wing's and the tail's share lifts on past it, as the Extra's (#935); was 0.2035.

n3_glide.source: L/D at 11 m/s, derived 8.18, 12 percent either way

n4_top.source: level speed at full throttle, derived 17.10, 10 percent either way: a 13 x 4's pitch speed is 19.2 m/s. Derived 23.58 since then, re-derived 2026-10-11 on APC's 13 x 4E curve (prop curves, npm run prop:curves -- wings), was 17.10 on the straight line; the same 10 percent about it. The pitch speed no longer caps it: APC's 13 x 4E thrust holds on past the geometric pitch, 19.2 m/s, and runs out at about 1.45 times it, so the top speed is mu 1.23 on the curve where the line stopped it at 0.89. Re-derived 2026-10-12 on the gates' 4.1 V seat (w36-seat-voltage: the pack's loaded voltage over the table's v_meas through the motor's law, scripts/lib/propcurve.js wingSeat): derived 26.67, was 23.58; the same 0.900 to 1.100 of it (was 21.22 to 25.94).

n5_roll.source: pb/2V at full aileron on the high rate, the flaps mixed in as full span ailerons, Clda throw_a / -Clp, derived 0.301 (373 deg/s at 13 m/s); 25 percent either way, the width the large deflection correction K' carries

n6_hover.source: hanging on the prop, the nose held up by the elevator and rudder in the slipstream, the height on the throttle: sqrt(W / T_static), derived 0.8015; 5 percent either way. The video's pilot hovers at about 55 to 65 percent by eye (07:38), a thumb on a radio whose throttle curve is not known; the plant's thrust goes as the stick squared, so this is the estimate's figure, not the video's Since 2026-10-11 the prop turns at sqrt(W / T_static), 0.8015 of full, at a duty of 0.7776 on the electric motor's own law, n^2 + 5.667 n = 6.667 d (plant_wing.c prop_spool, docs/FLIGHTMODEL.md "The electric throttle"); the same 5 percent about it. Re-derived 2026-10-12 on the gates' 4.1 V seat (w36-seat-voltage: the pack's loaded voltage over the table's v_meas through the motor's law, scripts/lib/propcurve.js wingSeat): derived 0.6665, was 0.7776; the same 0.950 to 1.051 of it (was 0.739 to 0.817). The prop still turns at sqrt(W / T_static), 0.8015 of full; on a 4.1 V pack loaded over the 3.401 V a cell the balance was taken at, the duty that turns it there is less.

n7_vertical.source: straight up at full throttle, where the thrust meets the weight and the zero lift drag, derived 6.60; 10 percent either way. Derived 11.12 since then, re-derived 2026-10-11 on APC's 13 x 4E curve (prop curves, npm run prop:curves -- wings), was 6.60 on the straight line; the same 10 percent about it. Re-derived 2026-10-12 on the gates' 4.1 V seat (w36-seat-voltage: the pack's loaded voltage over the table's v_meas through the motor's law, scripts/lib/propcurve.js wingSeat): derived 14.98, was 11.12; the same 0.900 to 1.100 of it (was 10.01 to 12.23).

n8_torque_roll.source: hanging at the hover throttle with the ailerons let go: the prop's 0.243 N m of reaction less the swirl's root and fin shares (SWIRL_KEEP 0.65, Selig AIAA 2010-7938), 0.153 N m, against the air the turning airframe sweeps through (rot_k roll), derived 210 deg/s to the left; 25 percent either way. The video's pilot holds a slower 75 deg/s with the ailerons (15:06). The fin meets the swirl the static jet brings it, slip_loss[2] (Deters, Ananda and Selig 2015, AIAA 2015-2265, figs. 15a and 15b; ~/Desktop/fdfpv-loop/research/wash-speed/WASH-SPEED.md), and SWIRL_KEEP holds Selig's 0.40 at 0.65 (was 0.74); was 216 at 0.161 N m, the band 162 to 270.

n9_aileron_hover.source: the same with full right aileron: the full span ailerons' inboard share in the slipstream, dp fa S b Clda throw_a, 0.239 N m, against the net torque, derived 159 deg/s right; 40 percent either way, the difference of two estimates. Without the flaps mixed in the ailerons start outside the slipstream and this is nothing. The fin meets the swirl the static jet brings it, slip_loss[2] (Deters, Ananda and Selig 2015, AIAA 2015-2265, figs. 15a and 15b; ~/Desktop/fdfpv-loop/research/wash-speed/WASH-SPEED.md), and SWIRL_KEEP holds Selig's 0.40 at 0.65 (was 0.74); was 151, the band 91 to 211.

n10_zero_speed.source: hanging still, full up elevator and full right rudder from rest: the wash's dp on the surfaces' immersed shares, saturating on a flat plate at the control's angle, derived 31.91 in pitch and 15.68 in yaw; 25 percent either way. With the prop stopped, under 5 percent of it. The tail meets dp less the static jet's spread, slip_loss (Deters, Ananda and Selig 2015, AIAA 2015-2265, figs. 15a and 17a; ~/Desktop/fdfpv-loop/research/wash-speed/WASH-SPEED.md): on the whole far wake it was 40.78 and 22.33, the band 30.6 to 51.0 and 16.7 to 27.9. Re-derived 2026-10-12 on the gates' 4.1 V seat (w36-seat-voltage: the pack's loaded voltage over the table's v_meas through the motor's law, scripts/lib/propcurve.js wingSeat): derived 54.58, was 40.78; the same 0.750 to 1.251 of it (was 30.6 to 51.0). The gate flies sqrt(W / T_static), 0.8015, the prop's speed share at the hover, as its stick; on the gates' 4.1 V pack that stick turns the prop to 22.29 N, 1.34 times the weight, and the wash's dp goes with the thrust (nighttimber:derive prints both). At the hover's own stick, 0.6665, it is 40.78 and 22.33 as before: the gate's stick, not the authority, moved. Re-derived 2026-10-12 on the gates' 4.1 V seat (w36-seat-voltage: the pack's loaded voltage over the table's v_meas through the motor's law, scripts/lib/propcurve.js wingSeat): derived 29.89, was 22.33; the same 0.748 to 1.249 of it (was 16.7 to 27.9). The rudder's the same way. Re-derived again 2026-10-12: the gate now flies the hover's own stick on the seated pack (wingSeat stickFor), so the authority is the derivation's at the hover thrust, unchanged, and the band is back to its pre-seat values. On the combined plant (w36-physics) the hover's own stick on the seated pack holds the thrust at the weight: nighttimber:derive gives 31.91 and 15.68 with the tail's slip_loss, this band.

n13_rest.source: E-flite's side photograph: the spinner's axis 4.5 deg nose up of the ground, the CG 0.2562 m up, 21.5 percent of the weight on the tailwheel; half a degree, 5 mm and 3.5 points either way

n14_takeoff.source: full throttle from standing with half flaps, the tail up at 5 m/s and the nose to 8 deg: liftoff at 8.5 m/s after 3.91 m (nighttimber:derive); 40 percent short and 60 long, the Extra's, since the plant's roll has the gear's springs and the pilot's hands in it and the derivation has neither. Derived 3.09 m (3.085), re-derived 2026-10-11 on APC's 13 x 4E curve (prop curves, npm run prop:curves -- wings), was 3.91 on the straight line; the same 40 percent short and 60 long about it. Re-derived 2026-10-12 on the gates' 4.1 V seat (w36-seat-voltage: the pack's loaded voltage over the table's v_meas through the motor's law, scripts/lib/propcurve.js wingSeat): derived 2.513, was 3.085; the same 0.600 to 1.601 of it (was 1.85 to 4.94).

n16_cross_host.source: the Night Timber's recorded take off, hover, torque roll and flight, state trace hash, Node against headless Chrome

n17_person_hover.source: can a person hover it, as the real one is hovered (analysis/3D-VIDEO-LESSONS.md, 07:38 and 15:00)? scripts/hover-probe.js's person paced pilot (0.2 s late, ten moves a second in fiftieths of the stick, McRuer and Jex), its 648 pilot grid, flying the video's technique: the ailerons hold a slow 75 deg/s torque roll rather than stopping it (study.mjs hoverLaw 'video'), in AS3X, the receiver as the aircraft ships. At least one pilot of the grid holds the nose within 20 deg of vertical and the height within 10 m for 10 s. The count is reported for Manual and AS3X, both techniques Re-posed 2026-10-12 (w37-fc-feel-3, lead decision): the receiver now flies the factory preset's ratios (EFL13850's .SRM, 34, 25 and 20) under the margin ceiling, and with them AS3X video holds 0 of 648, as Manual video does (0 of 648; stop it 4 Manual, 6 AS3X). The 1 of 648 it held before rode on the ceiling gains, a pitch and yaw damper three to thirteen times the factory tune's. The person pilot's hover the video's way is the known limit of that pilot (the hover lane's finding, as the lead relayed it 2026-10-12: that pilot's rudder loop cannot meet its margins), not the receiver's, so N17 now asks that AS3X be no worse than Manual for the person, each technique: AS3X's holders at least Manual's. minHolders is no longer judged. The video's human hover stays an open item (docs/NIGHTTIMBER-STAGE1.md).
